items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 73:1
items.html: Arich Anpin is entirely the aspect of Hochma. Indeed, in order to bestow, the Hochma must be clothed in Hassadim, for the lower ones do not receive Hochma except in a garment of Hassadim. And this bestowal of the illumination of Hochma in Hassadim is called the face of Arich Anpin, for the place of bestowal is called the face. But in its backside, where the Hochma is not clothed in Hassadim, it is called the back of the neck (Oref), or Kadla. That is, there is no place of bestowal from there to the lower ones below it, for they cannot receive from it without clothing in Hassadim; and if they received, the external ones would attach to the bestowal, for every illumination in which there is a deficiency, the external ones attach in the place of the deficiency, as is known. Hence the hairs of the head cover the back of the neck and delimit it, so that it bestows only through the hairs, as written in regard to the spikes of the hair. (Page 367, Item 152).
